passages.original: Unde et Joannes : Omnis qui facit justitiam, ex Deo est. Cujus participes sunt, pudicitia, castitas, et horum similia. ET PIE VIVAMUS, hoc est religiose. Ne enim immoderata sit justitia, pietas comitanda est » quae pars est justitiæ. Et siout beatus Augustinus dicit, Dei cultor intelligitur. IN HOC SÆCULO, id est in præsenti vita, propter illud quod Dominus ait: Qui perseveraverit usque in finem, hic salvus erit. Quae pietas ADVENTUM GLORIÆ ET SALVATORIS NOSTRI JESU CHRISTI exspectat, secura de fide et opere suo ; sicut e coatra impietas reformidat. BEATAM SPEM dicit caelestem patriam. Est enim spes exspectatio futurorum bonorum. Spes dicta est, quasi recte gradiendi pes. De qua Apostolus : Spes quæ videtur, non est spes. Contraria est illi desperatio, cui nulla est pœnitendi facultas. Quandiu enim homo peccalum amat, iuturam beatitudinem non sperat; sed ille fiducialiter exspectat, qui ejus praeceptis in omnibus obtemperat.
passages.english: Hence John also [says]: "Everyone who does justice is from God." Its companions are modesty, chastity, and things like these. AND LET US LIVE PIOUSLY, that is, religiously. For so that justice may not be immoderate, it must be accompanied by piety, which is a part of justice. And as blessed Augustine says, [piety] is understood as the worship of God. IN THIS WORLD, that is, in the present life, because of what the Lord says: "He who perseveres to the end will be saved." This piety awaits THE COMING OF THE GLORY AND OF OUR SAVIOUR JESUS CHRIST, secure in its faith and its work; just as, on the contrary, impiety dreads [it]. By BLESSED HOPE he means the heavenly homeland. For hope is the expectation of future goods. Hope (*spes*) is so called as if [from] the foot (*pes*) of walking rightly. Of it the Apostle [says]: "Hope that is seen is not hope." Opposed to it is despair, which has no capacity for repentance. For as long as a person loves sin, he does not hope for the future blessedness; but he awaits it with confidence who obeys His commands in all things.
passages.notes: Several scanning errors corrected silently (siout = sicut, e coatra = e contra, peccalum = peccatum, iuturam = futuram); the stray » after "comitanda est" omitted. The etymology spes / pes ("foot") is a wordplay not reproducible in English.
